title: How to Choose a Voice AI Partner for Your Bath Remodeling Call Center
summary: Comparing voice AI vendors for bath remodeling? Here's the checklist: integration, bath-specific conversations, time-to-live, and the team question.
body_markdown:
By[Pam Torrey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pam-torrey-920175b4/) , Senior Director of Marketing at Leaping AI


[Once you’ve decided you need a voice and SMS AI agent](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-for-bathroom-remodelers) and[not a chatbot or text-only tool](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-vs-chatbot-vs-sms-ai-for-contractors) , you’re confronted with a harder question: which vendor should you pick? This category doesn’t have a lot of the traditional markers of quality you look for in other software purchases. There aren’t a lot of businesses that have years of track record, reviews are going to be newer, and there are new players on the scene every day. On top of that, each vendor’s homepage makes roughly the same claims. Here’s what you actually need to check before you sign on with a new AI agent provider.


## Why this decision is harder than it looks


The AI vendors selling into home improvement and home services all claim to be built for the industries. And on paper, that appears to be true. The feature lists are pretty much identical—answer calls, book appointments, integrate with the CRM. What really differentiates one solution from another is whether the vendor understands what a bathroom remodeling call sounds like before you get on the demo with them, or if you’re going to have to help them understand that during the onboarding process, at your expense.


Bathroom remodelers will run into a few different kinds of vendors in the search for an AI voice tool. Some are large platforms that expanded into voice from an adjacent category. Hatch, now a part of Yelp after a January 2026 acquisition, is the most obvious example. Some are players built specifically for home services call centers, with Revin as the closest comparison. Others are single-trade specialists that know one vertical deeply and little else—roofing-focused tools like Alivo, or plumbing-focused like Broccoli fall into this camp. None of these is automatically the wrong fit, but each comes with a different set of trade-offs. It’s important to know them before the first discovery call, not after the contract has been signed.


## The buyer’s checklist: what matters


Integration with your existing tech stack. Your CRM and scheduling tools were expensive to purchase, time consuming to onboard, and integral to how you run your business. An AI voice and SMS vendor should plug into your existing technology instead of asking you to run a second system in parallel. Ask specifically which CRMs they’ve connected to in home improvement, and don’t accept “we integrate with most platforms” as a response. To learn more about how Leaping AI integrates with home improvement technology, check out our[guide to CRM integrations](https://leapingai.com/blog/voice-ai-crm-integration) .


Can it handle a bathroom remodeling conversation? Each conversation with a homeowner will be different, filled with nuance, whether the discussion is about a one-day tub-to-shower conversion, a full gut renovation, a wet-space conversion, or an accessibility upgrade for a homeowner aging in place. A generic home services script that doesn’t take these differences into account isn’t going to cut it. Ask the vendor to walk you through how the agent handles these different types of inquiries and ask for examples.


How long it takes to go live. You need to know the time to ramp up the new tool so you can plan on when you’ll see ROI. Ask for an onboarding plan and whether the implementation will be done virtually or in person.


What happens to your existing call center team? This is the question every call center manager and rep is going to ask the moment an AI voice agent is brought into the conversation. You need a real answer—a real plan for the people on your team.


## The “are you replacing my team” objection, answered honestly


The first real objection you will hear internally is about your team versus AI agents, and it deserves a real answer instead of a deflection. The honest pattern across contractors who have deployed voice and SMS AI in their call centers is redeployment of existing team members rather than replacement.


Lifetime Bath & Glass put a voice agent on[real-time outbound so leads get reached within 10 seconds](https://leapingai.com/blog/why-one-day-bath-companies-are-losing-jobs-to-a-missed-phone-call) of coming in. Their top-performing CSR was not replaced by that agent. She was promoted to customer success manager, handling the more complex calls and customer scenarios that require a human touch, while the AI agent takes care of the routine and repetitive calls.


That same pattern shows up across home improvement companies. Panda Exteriors, a roofing and siding company with a large canvassing program, had five CSRs tied up in confirming appointments for the face-to-face team. After they brought in AI voice to handle scheduling, those CSRs were redeployed into outbound telemarketing roles, generating direct revenue and dropping customer acquisition cost by 3%. The CSRs were repurposed for higher value, more complex work.


If a vendor doesn’t have specific examples of how their technology works alongside people, that’s worth noticing.


## What time-to-value should look like


Bath Experts, a Midwest bath remodeling company, launched their voice AI tool in just 30 days. Their agent handles about 4,000 outbound calls a day, reaches roughly 15% of the leads it dials, and books about 5 in-home consultations a day. Those appointments are worth somewhere between $5,000 and $30,000 to Bath Experts.


It is reasonable to ask your AI agent vendor for a specific onboarding plan to understand how long it will take from kickoff to launch. If the answer to the question “how long will it take to go live?” is something vague or the company sales rep hedges, ask about specifics. You can even ask to speak to an existing customer to understand what their onboarding process was like.


## A vendor-evaluation checklist you can screenshot


**What to ask**


**What a strong answer sounds like**


CRM and scheduling integration


Names the specific tools they’ve connected to in home improvement, rather than a vague “most platforms”


Bath-specific conversations


Can describe how the agent handles a full-gut inquiry differently than a one-day swap


Time to live


A specific number of weeks, with a reason behind it


Impact on your team


A real redeployment story, not just “don’t worry, it’s additive”


Voice quality


You can hear a real customer call, not just a scripted demo


Inbound and outbound coverage


Handles after-hours inbound and aged-lead outbound, not just one
